transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess… I’ve been arranging my days around avoiding elevators. Like taking five flights of stairs at home, skipping a workshop in a high-rise, and I stopped visiting one of my older computer students because his building doesn’t really have another way up.
What is it about elevators that feels frightening to you?

It’s… mostly the feeling that I could get stuck in there, or that it could drop. I know, logically, office elevators are probably safe, but when I see the older doors in my building or at work, my brain just kind of treats it like danger. Like it’s about to happen, even if I know that sounds a bit much.
Outside of elevators, do you also feel this kind of fear in other places where it might be hard to get out quickly, like buses, trains, tunnels, or crowded stores?
Not really… I mean, I haven’t noticed it with buses or stores or anything like that. It’s pretty much elevators that set it off.
When you have to use an elevator, do you suddenly get a rush of intense panic?
Yeah… pretty much right away. If I’m walking toward one, or I hear it open, my chest gets tight and my hands start sweating. It kind of hits before I can talk myself out of it.
Have you ever had one of these panic attacks out of the blue, when you weren’t near or thinking about an elevator?
I don’t think so. It’s usually tied to the elevator, or like… knowing I might have to use one.
